summary: Feed s155_double is degraded: NDR sees 19.0% one-way TCP sessions (92/485) and suffers microburst overload to 20.24 Gbps on a 10 Gbps port (202% capacity). Both prevent complete bidirectional session reconstruction and cause detection gaps.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of the same flow to the same NDR port. Likely asymmetric routing with RX/TX arriving on different TAPs/SPANs and forwarded to different tools, or a SPAN configured for one direction only, so only one side of the conversation reaches this NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, state tracking and detection. With 19% one-way sessions it cannot reconstruct flows, misses lateral movement/C2/exfiltration, and generates incomplete flow records.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate RX and TX of each 5-tuple to the same NDR tool port at the packet broker to restore full bidirectional visibility required for NDR detection.

findings.root_cause: Microburst of 20.24 Gbps in 1ms exceeds the 10 Gbps NDR port capacity by 2x. Packet broker is sending too much aggregate traffic to a single tool port without load balancing or filtering, causing buffer overrun and drops during bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port is oversubscribed (202% of capacity). Even with needs_full_payload=true, the tool will drop packets randomly during bursts, creating blind spots, missed alerts, and incomplete forensic capture. Sustained overload degrades NDR performance.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2-3 NDR ports (or higher-speed port) with flow-aware 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port load <80% and preserve full payload for NDR analysis; do not slice as NDR needs full payload.
